assumptions: The R-419 conditional law is positive and normalized and the projected conductance is symmetric and nonnegative.
The R-422 core/tail split is reused exactly with no row-dependent retuning of alpha or theta.
The sqrt(pi) transform preserves the finite weighted Dirichlet form and the block basis is formed from disjoint nonempty supports.
The residual block A_VV is positive on every eligible finite row, so the harmonic solve is well-defined.
The finite harmonic split is evaluated without rounding lower bounds upward, and the Lean lane is a scalar cross-check rather than a matrix formalization.
boundary: R-424 closes only the finite two-block harmonic Schur assembly and its residual reuse on the fixed Q3 grid. It does not close the Q3LOCK common-alpha or broken-sector coercivity parent gates.
evidence_level: T0 / exact finite harmonic coarse-Schur decomposition plus executed Q3-row assembly; no uniform theorem or physical conclusion
missing_assumptions: A cutoff-, volume-, phase- and exhaustion-uniform lower bound for both the coarse Schur and residual forms on one Hamiltonian common core.
A common split-limit map controlling the block-constant variables and residual coordinates under changing regulators and volumes.
Two-sided form-norm control of actual R-399 histories and a transfer theorem through the R-415 semigroup estimates.
Hamiltonian-to-OS/KMS/GNS identification and a sectorwise coercive estimate.
non_claims: No cutoff-, volume-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform coarse or residual bound.
No global Poincare or arbitrary-observable Schur theorem.
No common Hamiltonian core, common split rule or history transfer.
No OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction or sectorwise spectral gap.
No continuum, C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills or mass-gap conclusion.
